data.description:
## Goal

As the proxy operator I want to know, with evidence, whether the compaction
header bridge (option 2: proxy signals compaction, client mirrors the compacted
view) actually works end to end — and if it does not, to fix the specific
broken link — so that we stop carrying an "implemented" feature that changes
nothing.

`discovered-from: LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8` (producer, completed) and
`SorraAgents:SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0` (client bridge, deleted).

## Why this exists: the bridge has never run

An RCA on 2026-10-31 established that option 2 did not *fail* — it was never
executed. The mechanism is sound; the chain was never completed.

| # | Link | State | Evidence (verified 2026-10-31) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Proxy decides to compact | **DISABLED** | `proxy/config.yaml` `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0`; `proxy/proxy/compaction.py:873` returns `reason="compaction_disabled"` when `trigger <= 0`; 54,937 `compaction_bypass_eval … action=noop reason=compaction_disabled` in retained logs; **0** `action=compact`; usage report "No compactions observed in window" |
| 2 | Proxy emits `X-Compaction-*` | **cannot fire** | `proxy/proxy/router.py:410` gates on `session_result["compaction_applied"]`, set only at `router_helpers.py:5856` when `action=="compact" and applied and not dry_run`; **0** occurrences of the header name in retained logs |
| 3 | Pi surfaces response headers | works | `pi-coding-agent/dist/core/extensions/types.d.ts:707` (`AfterProviderResponseEvent {status, headers}`); Local Proxy uses `api: openai-completions`, whose transport passes `headersToRecord(response.headers)` on SSE responses |
| 4 | Bridge mirrors the view | installed, idle | symlink `~/.pi/agent/extensions/proxy-compaction-bridge` → `~/projects/SorraAgents/pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge` (target present); absent headers ⇒ deliberate no-op by contract |
| 5 | End-to-end validation | **never happened** | the SA audit failed on infrastructure (`audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated … no slot within 90s`, model output unparseable), recorded 8/8 ACs "partial", then the item was deleted; no gap item was raised |

Timeline defect: the bridge was implemented and symlinked **2026-09-17** with the
note *"headers are not yet emitted … live end-to-end validation is pending the
producer side"*; the producer shipped in **v0.1.19 on 2026-09-23**, and
server-side compaction was disabled **the same day** (LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6).
The overlap in which both halves were live was effectively zero.

## Secondary findings (would bite even with the signal on)

1. **No base handshake.** The contract is one-directional. The client rebuilds
   the base from its own JSONL (`custom_message` entries, `context_edit`
   omissions, tool results the proxy never stored); the proxy rebuilds from its
   own store. On disagreement `session_manager.py:451` sets
   `fallback_reason="history_mismatch"` → full reprocess and CREATION
   re-summarisation, i.e. exactly the churn the bridge exists to remove — and it
   fails **silently**.
2. **No runtime observability.** Header emission logs nothing (`router.py:430`
   is a `debug` on the failure path only) and the bridge logs nothing, so a
   loaded-but-idle extension is indistinguishable from a broken one.
3. **Ruled out:** marker role/shape is consistent on both sides — both use a
   user-role marker (`compaction.py:308`, `compaction-bridge.js:191`) and both
   build `system… + first_user + marker + tail` (`compaction.py:882`).

## Scope

Phase A — **prove the wire contract** (no client involved), then
Phase B — **prove the client mirror**, then
Phase C — **repair** whichever link fails, with the handshake and observability
below. Phase C is conditional on what A/B show; do not implement C speculatively.

In scope:
- Re-enabling the producer for a bounded, single-session probe and observing the
  four headers on a real response.
- Permanent INFO telemetry: one line per emission (proxy) and one per capture +
  one per reshape (bridge).
- If (and only if) A or B fails: base identity (`X-Compaction-Base-Id`
  emitted, `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` accepted) so divergence is detected explicitly
  instead of degrading into `history_mismatch`.

Out of scope:
- Pi-side native compaction (`~/.pi/agent/settings.json` `compaction.enabled`),
  which is the alternative, simpler route and a separate decision.
- Re-designing the summariser, compaction thresholds, or `turns_summarized`
  semantics.
- The local→remote boundary compaction hook (LP-0MVTDUBR00038ZRL).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 (Phase A): On a dedicated probe session, one response carries
  `X-Compaction-Occurred: true`, `X-Compaction-Marker`,
  `X-Compaction-Turns-Summarized`, `X-Compaction-Recent-Turns-Kept`, and the
  base64 marker decodes verbatim to the message the proxy injected (including
  the `The conversation history before this point was compacted into the
  following summary:` / `</summary>` delimiters). Test procedure T1.
- AC2 (Phase A, isolation): During T1 no session other than the probe session
  emits `compaction_event action=compact`, and the config is restored to
  `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0` before the item is closed. Test procedure T1
  steps 8–9.
- AC3 (Phase B): A live pi session crossing the trigger shows, in order: proxy
  `compaction_event … action=compact` → bridge "signal captured" → bridge
  "reshaped N→M messages" → next proxy request carrying the compacted base with
  **no** `history_mismatch` and **no** from-scratch re-summarisation. Test
  procedure T2.
- AC4 (observability, unconditional): the proxy logs one INFO per header
  emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and
  the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of
  the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".
- AC5 (Phase C, conditional): if the mirrored base diverges, the proxy detects
  it explicitly (base id mismatch, logged) instead of reporting
  `history_mismatch`, and re-signals exactly once; a second consecutive
  divergence stops mirroring for that session and logs why.
- AC6 (regression): with `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0` restored, no
  `X-Compaction-*` header is emitted, no bridge state is created, and the
  existing admission/routing decision path is unchanged (existing compaction and
  admission suites green).
- AC7: The item records a verdict — "option 2 viable" or "option 2 not viable,
  reason X" — with the T1/T2 log excerpts attached, so the earlier
  "implemented but inert" state cannot recur.

## Test instructions

### Preconditions (do not skip)

1. Proxy healthy: `curl -s --max-time 5 http://localhost:8080/v1/models | head -c 200`.
2. Summariser reachable — compaction summarises via
   `summarizer_model: {type: local, llama_model: Qwen2.5-7B}`
   (`proxy/config.yaml:1452`). If it is down, compaction returns
   `action=remote_with_guidance reason=summarizer_failed` and **no headers** are
   emitted; that is a precondition failure, not a bridge failure.
3. Confirm the starting state is disabled:
   `grep -c 'action=compact' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` → expect `0`.
4. **Safety:** `compaction_dry_run: false` (`proxy/config.yaml:1477`), so
   raising the ratio goes LIVE, not advisory. Contain the blast radius by
   pinning a dedicated `x-session-id` for the probe (compaction is per-session),
   and restore the ratio immediately after. Do not run this while a release or
   audit batch is in flight.

### T1 — prove the wire contract (deterministic, no pi involved)

1. Compute the trigger for the change you are about to make: with
   `local_model_ctx_size: 262144` and 2 slots, the per-slot clamp is
   `262144 // 2 - 4096 = 126976`; at ratio `0.7` the trigger is
   **88,883 tokens** (`compaction.py:226`). The probe session must exceed it and
   stay under the 120,000 warm routing cap, so target ~100k estimated tokens.
2. Enable the producer: set `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0.7` in
   `proxy/config.yaml`, then
   `curl -sX POST http://localhost:8080/admin/reload-config` → expect
   `{"status":"success",...}` and log line
   `Configuration reloaded successfully via admin endpoint`.
3. Build a 3-turn probe (≥88,883 estimated tokens, <120,000) with a unique
   session id:
   ```bash
   SID="rca-compaction-probe-$(date +%s)"
   python3 - "$SID" <<'PY'
   import json, sys
   sid = sys.argv[1]
   filler = ("RCA probe payload for the compaction header bridge. " * 7000)  # ~420 KB
   msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": filler + "
TURN 1"}]
   for n in (2, 3):
       msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": "ack"})
       msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": filler + f"
TURN {n}"})
   body = {"model": "code", "stream": True, "messages": msgs,
           "max_tokens": 16, "temperature": 0}
   open("/tmp/probe.json", "w").write(json.dumps(body))
   open("/tmp/probe.sid", "w").write(sid)
   print("session:", sid, "messages:", len(msgs), "chars:", sum(len(m["content"]) for m in msgs))
   PY
   ```
   Re-send this same body until the session crosses the trigger (the proxy logs
   the estimate per request as `compaction_bypass_eval … est_before=<n>`; check
   it with
   `grep 'compaction_bypass_eval' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log | tail -1`).
   Sending it twice from the same `x-session-id` is normally enough. Tune the
   `* 7000` multiplier if `est_before` lands outside 89k–119k.
4. Send request N and capture headers:
   ```bash
   curl -sS -N -D /tmp/h_N.txt -o /tmp/body_N.txt \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer not_needed" \
     -H "x-session-id: $(cat /tmp/probe.sid)" \
     -H "x-local-preference: local-preferred" \
     --data @/tmp/probe.json http://localhost:8080/v1/chat/completions
   ```
5. **Pass criterion A** — the response that compacts carries all four headers:
   ```bash
   grep -i '^x-compaction-' /tmp/h_N.txt
   # expect:
   # x-compaction-occurred: true
   # x-compaction-marker: <base64>
   # x-compaction-turns-summarized: <n≥1>
   # x-compaction-recent-turns-kept: <k>
   ```
6. **Pass criterion B** — the marker round-trips verbatim:
   ```bash
   grep -i '^x-compaction-marker:' /tmp/h_N.txt | cut -d' ' -f2- | base64 -d
   # must start with: The conversation history before this point was compacted into the following summary:
   # and end with:    </summary>
   ```
7. **Pass criterion C** — the proxy agrees it compacted live:
   ```bash
   grep -E 'compaction_event .*action=compact|session_compaction applied' \
        /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log | tail -4
   # expect action=compact, reason=compacted_within_target, dry_run=False,
   # and `session_compaction applied session=$(cat /tmp/probe.sid)`
   ```
   If instead you see `action=noop reason=below_trigger`, the probe is too small
   — go back to step 3. If `action=remote_with_guidance
   reason=summarizer_failed`, the precondition in 2 is broken.
8. Confirm isolation (AC2): `grep 'action=compact' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log
   | grep -v "$(cat /tmp/probe.sid)"` → expect empty.
9. Restore: `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0`, `curl -sX POST
   …/admin/reload-config`, then confirm the next request logs
   `reason=compaction_disabled` and the response carries no `X-Compaction-*`
   header. Delete the probe session:
   `curl -sX DELETE http://localhost:8080/admin/sessions/$(cat /tmp/probe.sid)`.

**T1 verdict:** if any of A/B/C fails, stop — the producer side is the defect and
Phase C is not needed yet. Record the raw headers and log lines on this item.

### T2 — prove the client mirror (pi session)

1. Add the AC4 logging to the bridge (`pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`):
   log in `handleResponse` (`signal captured session=… turns_summarized=…
   recent_turns_kept=… marker_chars=…`) and in `reshape` (`reshaped X→Y
   messages for session=…`, plus a no-op line `no signal — passthrough` when
   state is absent). Keep it to one line each, no payload bodies.
2. `/reload` in pi (or restart it). Confirm from pi's own log that the extension
   loaded; a load error here is itself a finding.
3. Start a fresh pi session on `Local Proxy/code`, re-enable the producer as in
   T1 step 2, and work turns until the session crosses 88,883 estimated tokens
   (paste a large file if you need to move fast; watch `est_before` in the proxy
   log).
4. **Pass criterion D** — ordering is visible and correct:
   proxy `compaction_event action=compact` → bridge `signal captured` →
   bridge `reshaped X→Y messages` (Y < X).
5. **Pass criterion E** — the next pi request carries the compacted base:
   in the proxy log the next `routing_estimate_session` / request for that
   session shows the reduced token count, **no** `history_mismatch`, and **no
   second from-scratch** `compaction_event` (incremental only: `turns_summarized`
   should stay small relative to the session, not reset to "everything").
6. **Fail signature to record verbatim** (this is RCA finding F4): any of
   `history_mismatch` on the following turn, `est_before` jumping back up to the
   pre-compaction value, or a repeated `action=compact` whose `turns_summarized`
   equals the whole session — i.e. the client's rebuilt base is not recognised
   as the proxy's base.
7. Restore `compaction_trigger_ratio: 0` and reload.

**T2 verdict:** pass ⇒ option 2 is viable, close with AC7's "viable" record (and
AC5 is not needed). Fail ⇒ Phase C: implement base identity
(`X-Compaction-Base-Id` = hash of the emitted base; client returns it as
`X-Dispatch-Base-Id`; proxy adopts a matching client base instead of
re-summarising, logs a mismatch once, and re-signals once).

## Evidence to attach on closure

- `/tmp/h_N.txt` header dump (redact the marker body, keep its length and the
  decoded first/last line).
- The matching `compaction_event` / `session_compaction applied` lines.
- The T2 bridge lines plus the following request's `est_before` /
  `history_mismatch` evidence.
- The restored-config check (AC6).

## Related

- LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8 (producer — headers), LP-0MU44KSMS002DBWA,
  LP-0MU44KR5F0015D7A (contract tests).
- LP-0MU61IRVC003RRN6 (disabled server-side compaction; reason this is inert).
- LP-0MTXGU9N1009QNSB (compaction not durable across turns),
  LP-0MTXEBQ4E001BMI2 (local HTTP 400 on compacted history).
- SorraAgents SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0 (client bridge, deleted; commits d6def7bb,
  16d2bd0c — code is present at `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/`).
- LP-0MVTDUBR00038ZRL (adjacent boundary-compaction mechanism).

data.description:
## Goal

As the proxy operator I want T1 (the wire-contract proof below) to be a single
deterministic command with a machine-readable verdict, so that AC1/AC2/AC6 are
repeatable at any time instead of being a hand-run sequence that has to be
re-derived from prose — and so the *next* regression is caught by re-running
one command.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8 (Phase A, test-first). Test procedure T1 in the
parent description is the specification.

## Why this is the first child (test-first)

The parent's T1 is currently a 9-step manual recipe with hard-coded `/tmp`
paths, a hand-tuned `* 7000` filler multiplier and no restore-on-failure
guarantee. `compaction_dry_run: false`, so an interrupted manual run leaves
`compaction_trigger_ratio: 0.7` live in production config. A harness with a
`finally` restore and a `--dry-run` mode is the prerequisite for executing
Phase A safely and for repeating it later.

## Scope

In scope:

- `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py`: preconditions, probe sizing, driving,
  header capture, marker verification, isolation check, restore, session delete,
  verdict JSON.
- `tests/test_compaction_bridge_probe.py`: unit tests for all pure helpers and
  the safety-critical paths.
- `--dry-run` (default-safe, CI-friendly) and `--live` (explicit opt-in).

Out of scope: the client mirror (Phase B), the bridge, base identity (Phase C).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py` runs T1 end to end in one command:
  preconditions (proxy `GET /v1/models` health, summariser reachable,
  `grep -c 'action=compact'` == 0), a unique pinned `x-session-id`, ported
  probe-body construction, repeated dispatch until `est_before` exceeds the
  trigger, response header + body capture, and `DELETE /admin/sessions/<id>`.
- AC2: The probe size is **computed, not hard-coded**: it calls
  `proxy.compaction.compaction_trigger_tokens` with the probe ratio
  (default 0.7) and asserts the computed trigger is 88,883 (per-slot clamp
  `262144 // 2 - 4096 = 126,976`), then sizes the body to land `est_before` in
  the band `[trigger + 1, 120000)` (the 120,000 warm-routing cap is a
  precondition guard, not a hard-coded constant).
- AC3: Config changes are always reverted. `compaction_trigger_ratio` is
  written to the probe ratio and restored to `0` in a `finally` block followed
  by `POST /admin/reload-config`, so an exception, timeout, Ctrl-C or failed
  criterion still leaves compaction disabled; the harness re-reads the config
  file afterwards and fails loudly if the restore did not take.
- AC4: `--dry-run` performs zero mutation and zero dispatch: it prints the
  computed trigger, target band, probe body size, chosen session id and the
  PlannedRequests, and exits `0`. It must be safe to run against a live proxy
  during a release.
- AC5: `--live` is required for any config write or dispatch; without it the
  harness refuses (non-zero exit, explicit message). The harness also requires
  an explicit `--no-batch-in-flight` acknowledgement so the "do not run during
  a release or audit batch" rule is enforced by the tool, not by memory.
- AC6: Marker round-trip is asserted verbatim: the `X-Compaction-Marker` base64
  decodes as UTF-8, starts exactly with `_SUMMARY_MARKER`, ends exactly with
  `_SUMMARY_MARKER_END`, and is non-empty; a failure records the decoded first
  and last 120 characters (never the whole body) for the evidence trail.
- AC7: The verdict is machine-readable JSON: booleans for criteria A (four
  headers present), B (marker round-trip), C (proxy logged live compaction),
  D (isolation — no other session compacted), E (config restored), plus the
  evidence file paths and the probe session id. Exit code is non-zero when any
  criterion is false.
- AC8: The redacted header dump written to the evidence directory keeps the
  marker's **length** and its decoded first/last line but not the marker body,
  matching the parent's "Evidence to attach on closure" requirement.
- AC9: Unit tests in `tests/test_compaction_bridge_probe.py` cover: trigger and
  body-size computation at ratios 0, 0.7 and 1.0; the header-parse matrix
  (all present / one missing / malformed base64 / non-numeric counts / wrong
  `occurred` value); the isolation filter (probe session excluded, a foreign
  session flagged as a failure); restore-on-exception; dry-run makes no
  network or filesystem-config calls (both stubbed and asserted un-called).
- AC10: The harness is never executed by the default test suite (it flips live
  config); the suite only exercises the unit tests and `--dry-run`.

## Minimal Implementation

- Reuse, do not reimplement: `proxy.compaction.compaction_trigger_tokens`,
  `compaction_target_tokens`, `_SUMMARY_MARKER` / `_SUMMARY_MARKER_END`,
  `proxy.utils.load_config`, and the existing `--json` conventions of
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` (argparse + verdict artefact +
  non-zero exit on failure).
- Structure the script as thin `main()` over pure helpers
  (`compute_probe_plan`, `parse_compaction_headers`, `check_isolation`,
  `redact_headers`, `restore_config`) so every unit test targets a helper, not
  `main()`. `--dry-run` exercises the same helper chain without the I/O.
- Drive requests with `httpx` (already a proxy dependency) rather than `curl`,
  so header capture is exact and the marker bytes are not shell-mangled.
- Write evidence into a caller-supplied `--evidence-dir` (default
  `docs/dev/compaction-bridge-probe-<ts>/`) so Phase A artefacts are
  reviewable and attachable to the parent, not stranded in `/tmp`.

## Deliverables

- `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py` (`--dry-run` / `--live`).
- `tests/test_compaction_bridge_probe.py`.
- Evidence directory layout documented in `--help`.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/compaction_bridge_probe.py`
- `tests/test_compaction_bridge_probe.py`
- `proxy/proxy/compaction.py`
- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `docs/session-compaction-design.md`

## Evidence (verified during planning)

- `compaction_trigger_tokens("medium", config)` with `ratio=0.7`,
  `local_model_ctx_size=262144`, `slots=2` returns **88883** (verified
  2026-10-31 in this worktree; the parent's arithmetic is correct).
- `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold = 120000` (the probe's upper bound).
- `server.compaction_trigger_ratio: 0`, `server.compaction_dry_run: false`.

## Dependencies

None. Prerequisite for the T1 execution child.

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want one INFO log line per compaction-header emission
(and one distinguishable line when compaction was evaluated but emitted
nothing), so that reading the proxy log tells me whether the signal was
emitted at all — closing secondary finding 2 of the parent ("Header emission
logs nothing ... a loaded-but-idle extension is indistinguishable from a broken
one") and satisfying AC4's proxy half.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — this is required whether or not
Phase A/B pass.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `proxy/proxy/router.py:397` `_build_compaction_headers()` returns `{}` or the
  header dict; the only log statement in it is
  `logger.debug("Failed to build compaction headers; omitting", ...)` on the
  exception path (`router.py:430`). The success path logs nothing.
- `router.py:2336` applies it with `outgoing_headers.update(...)` on the
  streaming path; a second site near `router.py:3551` covers the buffered path.
- `router_helpers.py:6218` already logs `session_compaction applied
  session=… priority=… est_before=… est_after=…` — but that line proves
  *compaction happened*, not that *headers were emitted*. The two can diverge
  (e.g. `compaction_summary_text` empty → no headers, compaction still
  applied).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: On the live-applied path, exactly one INFO line per response is logged:
  `compaction_headers emitted session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`. It is logged once per response on
  both the streaming (SSE) and buffered response paths — never once per SSE
  chunk.
- AC2: A response that evaluated compaction but emitted no headers logs exactly
  one line naming the reason, distinguishable from "emitted": one of
  `compaction_headers none reason=disabled|below_trigger|noop|dry_run|
  remote_with_guidance|no_summary_text|build_failed`. `no_summary_text` covers
  the real divergence case (compaction applied, summary missing) and
  `build_failed` covers the exception path.
- AC3: No header-emission line is emitted for requests that never reach the
  compaction path (e.g. remote dispatch with no session), keeping router log
  volume unchanged for the overwhelmingly common `compaction_disabled` case at
  a rate that permits long-window analysis (the `session_compaction applied`
  line already fires per compacted request; the new line must not multiply
  log volume for non-compaction traffic).
- AC4: The fail-safe contract is unchanged and better observed: an exception
  while building headers still yields no headers and never changes dispatch,
  but is now logged at **WARNING** with `exc_info=True` (was `debug`), so a
  silently broken emission is visible in normal operation.
- AC5: Header names, values and encodings are untouched:
  `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` passes **unmodified**.
- AC6: Unit tests assert: the AC1 line and each field on both response paths;
  exactly one AC1 line per response with a multi-chunk SSE stream; the AC2
  reason line for `disabled` / `below_trigger` / `dry_run` /
  `remote_with_guidance` / `no_summary_text`; WARNING + `exc_info` on the
  exception path; and that a logging failure cannot raise out of the emission
  path (fail-safe preserved).
- AC7: No marker text, no summary body and no message content appear in any
  log line — only ids, counts and lengths.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a module-level helper in `proxy/proxy/router.py` next to
  `_build_compaction_headers` — e.g. `_log_compaction_headers(session_id,
  headers, reason=None)` — and call it from the two `outgoing_headers.update(
  _build_compaction_headers(...))` sites, so the accounting is in one place
  and both paths are testable with the existing `_mock_upstream_response`
  fixtures.
- Derive `reason` where the decision is already known rather than re-deriving
  it: `_build_compaction_headers` can return `(headers, reason)` internally
  while keeping its public single-dict behaviour, or the caller can read
  `session_result["compaction_reason"]` / `compaction_applied`. Prefer the
  minimal change that does not alter the contract test's public seam.
- Session id is already available at both call sites (`session_id`); truncate
  to 8 chars like the existing `session_compaction applied` line does, so
  operator greps work across both lines.
- `marker_chars` is `len(marker_b64)` (the header value length), which is what
  the parent's AC4 asks for ("marker length").

## Deliverables

- Emission telemetry in `proxy/proxy/router.py` on both response paths.
- Unit tests in `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` (extend) or
  a new `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_telemetry.py` (preferred: keeps the
  frozen contract file untouched per AC5).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_telemetry.py`
- `docs/session-compaction-design.md`

## Dependencies

None. Required by the T1 execution child (its pass criteria C/D are read from
these lines) and by the parent's AC4.

## Goal (user story)

As on-call, I want decode tokens/sec to be attributable to how many local
streams shared the decode batch, so the single-slot decode-latency prediction
(effects E3/E5) can be confirmed or refuted from metrics rather than reasoned
about.

## Context

`docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` §5.4 (E5) states the decode tail should
narrow at one slot because two streams no longer share the batch, and §5.8
lists this as unmeasurable with today's data. `llama_token_rate_gauge` is
labelled by `session_id` only (`proxy/proxy/metrics.py`), and the report's
`Decode speed` table is per stream, so nothing joins a decode rate to the
concurrency it was measured under.

`discovered-from:LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ` (single-slot impact audit).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A decode-rate histogram carries the concurrent-local-stream count (or
  pool occupancy at sample time) as a label, so a query can compute decode
  rate by concurrency bucket.
- AC2: The label/bucket source is the same slot-pool occupancy the sampler
  already reads (no second, divergent definition of concurrency).
- AC3: A unit test asserts the observed concurrency is attached to a sampled
  rate and that it reflects a two-stream and a one-stream case.
- AC4: A usage-analysis report metric derives decode tok/s per concurrency
  bucket and is documented in the REFERENCE.
- AC5: No change to scheduling or batching behaviour.

## Appendix

### Clarifying questions and answers

- Q: What is the authoritative concurrency source? A (plan): Use the existing
  `llama_slots_busy` gauge — it records "slots processing a task in the last
  successful /slots sample", which is the same pool occupancy the sampler
  reads. No new concurrency definition.
- Q: Does this change scheduling? A: No. AC5 requires no change to scheduling
  or batching behaviour. Only observability metrics are added.
- Q: What concurrency levels to bucket? A: Integer bucket counts (1, 2, 3+) —
  no complex histogram binning needed. The `llama_slots_busy` value at sample
  time is the count.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the local status paths to fail *closed* on an unknown
pool size instead of advertising three slots, so a missing config key can never
make capacity look larger than it is.

## Context

`docs/dev/single-slot-impact.md` §1.2 item 5 and §3.4 row 26
(LP-0MVTV6GA8002P7QU) record that three call sites read
`server_cfg.get("session_slot_pool_size", 3) or 3`
(`proxy/proxy/handlers.py` — the `/llama/local/status` idle and
total-slot paths), so an absent key advertises three slots at either geometry.
The literal predates the single-slot question and is a latent observability
defect, not a live one: the configured value wins whenever the key is present.

`discovered-from:LP-0MVTF26NP003KXKJ` (single-slot impact audit).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The three call sites no longer fall back to a literal slot count: they
  derive the pool size from the same helper the rest of the proxy uses (or
  report `unknown`/`0` explicitly) and never invent `3`.
- AC2: A unit test asserts that with `session_slot_pool_size` absent the
  status payload does not advertise 3 slots, and that a configured value is
  reported unchanged.
- AC3: The comment that documents the fallback behaviour is updated.
- AC4: No behaviour change when the key is present (the configured value is
  still reported verbatim).

data.description:
# Provide a script that deploys Grafana, safely, so the memory dashboard is viewable

**Headline:** add one idempotent, verifiable script (`scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`)
that installs the documented Grafana version, provisions the Prometheus
datasource and the `LLama Server Memory` dashboard, installs the systemd user
unit from `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service`, exposes it on loopback plus
tailnet only, and sets a non-default admin password from a `0600` file — so that
"how do I view the dashboard?" has a one-command answer instead of a manual
runbook with three latent defects.

## Problem statement

Grafana is **not installed on this host at all** (`~/bin/grafana` does not
exist, no `grafana-server.service` unit, nothing listening on `:3000`), so the
dashboard in `monitoring/` cannot be viewed. Today the only route is the manual
runbook in `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` + `monitoring/README.md` § 4,
and that runbook carries defects that a script would otherwise inherit:

1. **Wildcard bind.** The documented unit passes no `http_addr`, so Grafana
   binds `:3000` on **all** interfaces — LAN-reachable, which is wider than the
   tailnet-only boundary Prometheus deliberately uses
   (`monitoring/README.md` § *Exposure boundary*).
2. **Default credentials.** The doc instructs `admin`/`admin` and its
   verification commands hard-code `curl -u admin:admin`; the README § 4 says
   "change the admin password first" as prose that nothing enforces.
3. **A dashboard provider path that cannot resolve.**
   `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` sets
   `options.path: ${grafana_home}/conf/provisioning/dashboards`. Grafana
   interpolates `${...}` from the **process environment**, and no
   `grafana_home` variable exists, so the provider points at an unresolved path
   and the dashboard silently never loads. The existing test
   (`test_dashboard_provider_points_to_existing_dir`) *requires* the
   `${grafana_home}` token, so it protects the defect.
4. **Nothing verifies the outcome.** No test or script checks that the
   dashboard actually appears in Grafana's own API (`/api/search?type=dash-db`)
   or that its panels return data; the prior deployment item
   (LP-0MQR554O60033BGF) asserted "Grafana running" on paper while no
   Grafana was ever deployed.

## Users

Primary user: the operator of this host, who wants to open the memory dashboard
in a browser without hand-editing systemd units or re-deriving the exposure
decision each time.

User stories:

- As the host operator, I want **one command** that installs and starts Grafana
  with the Prometheus datasource and the `LLama Server Memory` dashboard
  already provisioned, so that I can open the dashboard immediately afterwards.
- As the host operator, I want the service bound to loopback and the tailnet and
  **never** to the LAN, with a non-default admin password held in a `0600`
  file, so that deploying a dashboard does not widen the attack surface.
- As the host operator, I want `--check` to tell me whether the deployment is
  healthy without changing anything, so that I can diagnose drift (unit
  disabled, service dead, datasource missing, dashboard absent) quickly.
- As a reviewer, I want the deploy path covered by tests that fail on the three
  defects above (wildcard bind, `admin/admin`, unresolvable provider path), so
  that they cannot silently return.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **A committed, idempotent script exists.**
   `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh` exists, is executable, declares its interface in
   a header comment, passes `bash -n` and `shellcheck` (already used by
   `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh`, `scripts/llama-bench.sh`), and follows the
   repository's install-script conventions (`set -euo pipefail`,
   `SCRIPT_DIR`/`REPO_ROOT` derivation, `--check` and `--quiet` flags as in
   `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`). Re-running it on an already-deployed host
   makes no change and exits `0`.

2. **It installs the documented Grafana version reproducibly.**
   The version is a single variable in the script and matches the version
   documented in `monitoring/README.md` (11.6.0); the tarball's published
   SHA-256 is verified before extraction; extraction lands in `~/bin/grafana`
   (the path `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` already uses) and the
   version is re-checked from the installed binary (`grafana-server -v`)
   afterwards. A checksum mismatch aborts non-zero without touching an existing
   installation.

3. **Provisioning files are installed, and the dashboard actually loads.**
   The script installs the datasource config, the dashboard provider config and
   the dashboard JSON into Grafana's provisioning directories, writing the
   provider `options.path` as a **concrete absolute path** (no unresolved
   `${grafana_home}` token). Success is asserted from Grafana's own API, not
   from file presence: `GET /api/health` reports `"database": "ok"`, the
   `Prometheus` datasource is present, and `GET /api/search?type=dash-db`
   returns the `LLama Server Memory` dashboard. The repo copies of
   `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` and
   `monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` stay the source of truth and
   the two dashboard JSON copies stay byte-identical.

4. **Exposure is loopback + tailnet, never LAN.** The installed unit/config
   binds Grafana to `127.0.0.1:3000` (the process never listens on a wildcard
   address), and tailnet access is provided by Tailscale's own listener rather
   than by widening Grafana's bind. The script derives the tailnet addresses at
   run time (`tailscale ip -4` / `ip -6`) instead of hard-coding them, degrades
   to loopback-only with a warning when Tailscale is down or `tailscale serve`
   is unavailable, and its own verification asserts that the LAN address
   (`192.168.0.199:3000`) is refused. No `admin`/`admin` credential appears
   anywhere in the script, the unit doc or the verification commands.

5. **The admin password is generated once and never committed.** On first run
   the script generates a strong password into `~/.config/grafana/admin.pass`
   with `0600` permissions (creating the directory `0700`), points Grafana at it
   via a file-based secret setting (never on the command line, never in the unit
   file, never in the repo), and reuses it on subsequent runs. The `--check`
   mode verifies the file exists with safe permissions and that authentication
   with the stored credential succeeds, reporting the credential **path** only —
   the value is never printed or logged.

6. **The unit is installed from the documented unit, not copied.** The script
   installs `~/.config/systemd/user/grafana-server.service` by extracting the
   ```` ```ini ```` block from `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` (the
   `unit_from_doc` pattern the repo already documents for every other unit),
   then `daemon-reload`, `enable --now`, and reports `is-active`. It aborts with
   a clear message if Prometheus (`127.0.0.1:9090`) is not answering, since a
   dashboard with a dead datasource is worse than no dashboard. The unit doc is
   updated in the same commit so the repository and the running state cannot
   drift.

7. **`--check` is a real health probe with documented exit codes.** Exit `0`
   when installed, enabled and active, health `ok`, datasource present,
   dashboard present, password file safe, LAN refused; exit `1` with a
   per-check failure list otherwise; exit `0` with a "not deployed" report only
   when `--check` is asked to inspect an undeployed host and `--allow-absent` is
   passed. Behaviour on an undeployed host is asserted by a test.

8. **Tests cover the script and the three latent defects.**
   `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` (or a sibling module) gains
   behavioural tests that: run `bash -n` and `shellcheck` over the script; drive
   the unit-extraction helper against `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` and
   assert the extracted unit has no wildcard listen address and no inline
   credential; run the script's provider-config rendering and assert the emitted
   `options.path` is absolute and exists; and grep the script, unit doc and README
   for `admin:admin` (or a `GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=admin` form) and fail on
   any hit. Reintroducing any of the three defects must fail at least one test;
   the obsolete `test_dashboard_provider_points_to_existing_dir` token
   requirement is replaced by an assertion that the provider path resolves.

9. **Documentation matches reality.** `monitoring/README.md` § 4 becomes "deploy
   with `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`", listing the script's commands, the exposure
   decision and the password-file location (path only); the "What runs here"
   table's `grafana-server.service` row stops saying "not running on this host"
   once deployed and instead documents how to start/stop/check it;
   `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` carries the binding, password and
   provisioning decisions the script implements; and any README section listing
   host scripts mentions the new one.

10. **The full project test suite passes** via `/skill:test`, with no
    regressions, and the change is exercised end-to-end once on this host
    (dashboard reachable over the tailnet, panels returning data for
    `gpu_gtt_used_bytes` and the proxy panels) with the outcome recorded in a
    comment on this item.

## Constraints

- **No new exporter, no Prometheus change.** `monitoring/prometheus.yml`, the
  rule files and the scrape jobs are untouched; this item only consumes
  `127.0.0.1:9090`.
- **Never widen the boundary.** No wildcard `:3000` bind, no LAN exposure, and
  no secrets in the repository, the unit file or the process command line.
- **No hand-edited units.** `~/.config/systemd/user/*.service` is produced from
  `docs/systemd/*.service`, never edited in place — the repository is the source
  of truth (`monitoring/README.md` § *Changing the boundary*).
- **No containers.** Host-first binary install, matching every other unit in
  this stack.
- **Downloaded artefact integrity is not optional.** A release tarball is only
  used after its published SHA-256 verifies.
- **Scripts live in `scripts/`**, use the repository's bash conventions, and
  degrade gracefully (never leave a half-installed unit enabled).
- UK English in all written output; **CHANGELOG.md is out of scope** (the ship
  pipeline manages it).

## Existing state (evidence, gathered 2026-10-31)

| Fact | Command / path | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| Grafana binary absent | `ls -d ~/bin/grafana` | *No such file or directory* |
| Grafana unit absent | `ls ~/.config/systemd/user/grafana-server.service` | *No such file or directory* |
| Service inactive, port free | `systemctl --user is-active grafana-server.service`; `ss -tln \| grep :3000` | `inactive`; nothing listening |
| Tailscale usable, `serve` unused | `tailscale serve status`; `tailscale ip -4/-6` | `No serve config`; `100.79.231.101`, `fd7a:115c:a1e0::9b33:e765` |
| Prometheus is the peer service | `ss -tln \| grep :9090` | `127.0.0.1:9090`, `100.79.231.101:9090`, `[fd7a:…]:9090` |
| Dashboard artefact | `monitoring/grafana_llama_memory_dashboard.json` | title `LLama Server Memory`, `version: 2`, panels: RSS, models loaded, 5xx rate, GPU memory (GTT + VRAM carve-out) |
| Provider path defect | `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` | `options.path: ${grafana_home}/conf/provisioning/dashboards` |
| Test protecting the defect | `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py:666` | asserts the path starts with `${grafana_home}` or `/` |
| Weak unit test | `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py:928` | `TestGrafanaSystemdUnit` only checks the file exists, is section-valid and mentions "grafana" |
| Documented install path | `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` | `/home/rgardler/bin/grafana/bin/grafana-server --homepath=/home/rgardler/bin/grafana --config=…/conf/defaults.ini`; no `http_addr`; `cp`-based setup; verification uses `admin:admin` |

## Desired change

New `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`:

```
Usage: scripts/deploy_grafana.sh [--check] [--allow-absent] [--quiet] [--version X.Y.Z]

  (default)        install + provision + enable + start + verify
  --check          verify only; never changes anything
  --allow-absent   with --check, exit 0 when Grafana is simply not deployed
  --quiet          report failures only
  --version        override the pinned Grafana version (default: 11.6.0)
```

Structure (mirrors `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh`):

1. `install` — download + SHA-256 verify + extract to `~/bin/grafana`; create
   `~/.local/share/grafana/data`, `~/.local/state/grafana/logs`,
   `~/.config/grafana` (`0700`).
2. `secret` — generate `/etc`-free `~/.config/grafana/admin.pass` (`0600`,
   32-byte base64) if absent; never overwrite, never echo.
3. `provision` — write `conf/provisioning/datasources/datasources.yaml` from
   `monitoring/grafana/datasources/`, and `conf/provisioning/dashboards/`
   provider config from `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` with
   `options.path` replaced by the real absolute directory, plus the dashboard
   JSON copies from `monitoring/`.
4. `unit` — extract the `ini` block from
   `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` into
   `~/.config/systemd/user/grafana-server.service`; `daemon-reload`;
   `enable --now`; `is-active`.
5. `expose` — `tailscale serve --bg --tcp=3000 http://127.0.0.1:3000` when
   Tailscale is up (with a warning + loopback-only fallback otherwise).
6. `verify` — `/api/health` = ok; datasource present; dashboard searchable by
   title; authenticated query through the datasource; `ss -tln` shows only
   loopback; LAN address refused.

Unit doc change: keep `ExecStart` as the documented binary path with
`--homepath`/`--config`, and add `Environment=` lines carrying only the two
binding overrides (`GF_SERVER_HTTP_ADDR=127.0.0.1`,
`GF_SERVER_HTTP_PORT=3000`) and the secret's **path**
(`GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD__FILE=%h/.config/grafana/admin.pass`). Neither the
secret value nor a second copy of it ever appears in the unit, the process
command line, or the journal.

## Key files (predicted)

- `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh` — new; the whole deployment above.
- `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` — binding + secret + provisioning flags;
  setup commands replaced by "run `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`".
- `monitoring/grafana/dashboards/dashboards.yaml` — provider path that resolves.
- `monitoring/README.md` — § 4 rewritten around the script; "What runs here"
  table row updated.
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — script tests, defect guards,
  `TestGrafanaSystemdUnit` strengthened, `test_dashboard_provider_points_to_existing_dir`
  replaced.
- `proxy/README.md` — script list entry (if it lists host scripts).

## Related work

- **LP-0MQR554O60033BGF** — Deploy Prometheus and Grafana instances (completed):
  its AC 2 says "Grafana running", but only Prometheus was ever deployed; this
  item closes that gap for real.
- **LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T** — Grafana dashboard GPU VRAM panel queries
  `rocm_vram_*` (in_review): made the dashboard deployable-by-review (panel
  queries now match published series); this item is what makes it *viewable*.
  Its guard (`TestGrafanaDashboardVramPanel`) must keep passing.
- **LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT** — deployable, tailnet-exposed Prometheus (epic): the
  exposure model this script must match.
- **LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G** — Docs: record the deployed monitoring stack and its
  tailnet-only exposure (completed): `monitoring/README.md` § 4, where the new
  commands belong.
- **LP-0MVQ6NQU9009LY2Y** — Stale monitoring references (open): adjacent docs
  churn; avoid conflicting edits to `proxy/README.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: exposure regression.** A convenience wildcard bind would silently undo
  the boundary work in LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT. Mitigation: ACs 4 and 8 assert
  loopback-only listening and LAN refusal, and the unit doc carries the flag.
- **Risk: secret leakage.** A password in the command line is visible in
  `ps`/`systemctl cat`/journal. Mitigation: file-based secret with `0600`, value
  never printed; AC 5 and AC 8's grep guard.
- **Risk: a green script over a broken dashboard.** File-copy success does not
  mean Grafana loaded the dashboard (see the `${grafana_home}` defect).
  Mitigation: AC 3 asserts via `/api/search`; `--check` re-asserts.
- **Risk: half-installed host.** A failure between `enable` and `verify` leaves
  a crash-looping unit. Mitigation: install → provision → unit → start →
  verify ordering, with the unit enabled only after provisioning succeeds, and
  the failure path stopping the unit and naming the remediation.
- **Risk: upstream artefact unavailability.** Grafana tarball URLs move between
  versions. Mitigation: single pinned version variable, checksum verification,
  and a clear abort message; the script never falls back to an unverified
  download.
- **Assumption:** `tailscale serve` is acceptable for tailnet exposure and the
  tailnet permits it (no serve config exists today; HTTPS certs may need
  enabling in the admin console — see open questions). Fallback is
  `http_addr=<tailnet IPv4>`, which loses loopback access and is therefore the
  documented second choice, not the default.
- **Assumption:** Grafana remains a single-operator, unauthenticated-to-the-
  tailnet service like Prometheus; no Alertmanager, no LDAP, no orgs.
- **Scope-creep watch:** proxy-side metric defects are out of scope
  (`llama_process_rss_bytes` publishing `0` is LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48 territory);
  a GTT-as-fraction panel remains the open follow-up noted in
  LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T. Neither is fixed here.

## Open questions (non-blocking) and decisions taken

- **Q: How is tailnet exposure provided?** — **Decision (agent, recommended):**
  bind Grafana to `127.0.0.1:3000` only and publish it with `tailscale serve`
  (`--bg --tcp=3000`), because Grafana's `http_addr` accepts a *single* address
  and cannot reproduce Prometheus's loopback+tailnet multi-bind. This keeps the
  process loopback-only (the principle behind the exporters) and puts the
  network boundary in Tailscale, where the device authentication already lives.
  Fallback if `tailscale serve` is unavailable: `http_addr=<tailnet IPv4>`, with
  loopback access lost and documented as the trade-off. **Reviewer should say so
  now if they prefer the fallback.**
- **Q: Does the tailnet have HTTPS/MagicDNS enabled** (needed for
  `tailscale serve --https=443`)? — Unverified from the host; `--tcp=3000` is the
  cert-free default and avoids the dependency. If HTTPS is available, an
  `--https` mode can be a follow-up.
- **Q: Does the admin password live in a unit `EnvironmentFile` or a Grafana
  secret file?** — **Decision (agent):** use Grafana's file-based secret setting
  (`GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD__FILE`) pointing at the `0600` password file, so
  no secret is duplicated into a unit environment file that `systemctl cat`
  would print.
- **Q: Should the script manage a `grafana.ini`?** — **Decision (agent):** no;
  keep `--config` at `conf/defaults.ini` and express the two overrides
  (`http_addr`, `http_port`) plus the secret via environment variables in the
  documented unit, so the repository stays the single source of truth.
- **Q: Should the script touch Prometheus?** — No. It only probes
  `127.0.0.1:9090` and refuses to deploy against a dead datasource.

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

Intake (2026-10-31) — no blocking questions asked: the operator's request was
"create a work item to build a script to deploy it", and the surrounding
evidence (absent install, documented-but-unsafe runbook, three latent defects,
`tailscale serve` unused) fixes the shape of the change. Decisions recorded
above for audit; each cites its evidence:

- *Which Grafana version?* — 11.6.0, the version `monitoring/README.md:23`
  documents and `docs/systemd/grafana-server.service` assumes.
- *Where does the script live?* — `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh`, next to
  `install_git_hooks.sh` / `install-cron.sh` / `install-rocm.sh`, with the same
  `--check`/`--quiet` convention and `set -euo pipefail` header.
- *Why not simply commit a `grafana.ini`?* — because the repo's units are the
  source of truth and are installed by extracting the `ini` block from docs;
  a second config file would be another copy to drift.
- *How is "it worked" proven?* — Grafana's own APIs (`/api/health`,
  `/api/datasources`, `/api/search?type=dash-db`) plus a datasource query, not
  file presence; tests assert the script does this.
- *What about the LAN?* — refused by test, by `--check`, and by the unit's
  loopback bind; the LAN address `192.168.0.199:3000` must return `000`.

## Goal

As the operator, I want the local-share gap attributed to *throughput* (not routing) and the costed options ranked, so the parent's aggregate-share target is set against what the hardware can actually deliver.

## Measured basis (2026-11-01 13:12:48-14:00:03, 1788 requests, 58 sessions)

- Offered prompt load: 125.6M prompt tokens in 47.25 min = ~44,300 prompt tokens/s.
- Local delivered: 877,908 prompt tokens over 46 streams in 1,223 s of busy time = ~718 tok/s.
- Routing is NOT the binding constraint: the refusals decompose into prompt-cost verdicts (large_context_bypass 32.8% of fallbacks, resident_prefix_insufficient 24.7%, local_admission_guard 18.1% incl. prefill_budget_exceeded 193/314 guard rejects, context_too_large 16.6%), and only 76 of 314 guard refusals had a free prefill gate — of which all but 20 exceeded the queue budget on their own measured ETA.
- Ceiling: one serialised prefill gate x 2,820 s x ~718 tok/s = ~2.0M prompt tokens/window = 2.3x today's local tokens => local share ceiling ~5.8%. A >=10% share would need ~4.2M local prompt tokens, i.e. >2x the whole window's single-gate capacity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — Costed options are compared: (a) session size/compaction (the median request is 57k new tokens; the top decile is >100k), (b) prefill-serialisation trade-off revisited with current-generation measurements, (c) model/quantisation or ctx/slot-geometry changes, (d) accepting the ~5.8% ceiling and re-scoping the parent's AC9 target. Each option carries a measured or explicitly-estimated tok/s and slot-hour cost.
- [ ] AC2 — A recommended target for the parent LP-0MVWEZCB0006WPBQ AC9 share is proposed with the arithmetic, and the recommendation is recorded as a comment on the parent.
- [ ] AC3 — No routing/config change is made by this item (read-only evaluation; changes become children).

## Constraints

- Do not merely widen the local context window (LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM already evaluated the ctx-size axis).
- Do not use 'forcing full prompt re-processing' as evidence of a cache defect (expected on Qwen3.x hybrid/SWA, see project AGENTS.md).

# Extend the status builder's live-work attribution during prefill (72 residual saturated-without-live-work polls)

Follow-on item filed from the **LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1** verification verdict (2026-11-01 night window), **re-targeted 2026-11-02 after log-analysis evidence corrected the attribution** (see Evidence below).

**Verdict (unchanged):** EXPECTED IMPROVEMENT ACHIEVED: NO — 72 saturated-without-live-work polls (0.41 %) remain, up from the 12-poll / 0.11 % AC4 residual baseline (+60 polls) though down from the 247-poll / 2.12 % pre-fix baseline. The abandoned_busy annotation IS firing (367 polls / 2.06 %), so the shift is real. Of the 72 residual polls, 65 were **tool-attributed** to `session_evicted` (nearest event within the 600 s lookback), 1 to `no_progress_watchdog`, 1 to `prefill_deadline`, and 5 were unattributable (2026-11-01 22:12:58, 22:13:00 ×2, 23:02:37, 23:03:32).

## Problem statement

A slot that is genuinely busy prefilling a real local dispatch reports `capacity_hint=saturated` with empty live-work fields (`local_in_flight_requests=0`, `local_owner_session_id=None`, `local_active_query=false`) on fresh slot detail, so consumers cannot tell the slot is doing live work. The measured residual is 72 polls / 0.41 % of the 2026-11-01 night, all attributable to status-builder attribution lag during prefill rather than to the post-cancel draining-ghost class the abandoned_busy fix (LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM) already closes.

## Evidence (log-analysis, 2026-11-01 night episode 05:26–05:33)

The original "session-eviction path" reading was a **nearest-event mis-attribution** — the eviction was not draining when the residual polls were read:

1. 05:26:46.361 `Evicted 2 expired/invalidated session(s)` → `lease_released` ×2 (`session_evicted`). Both slots were **already free 7 s later**: 05:26:53.850 status reads `available_slots=2`, `capacity_hint=idle`, `in_flight=0`. No draining ghost existed from this eviction.
2. 05:27:10.829 a NEW local dispatch begins: `[local] POST slot=0 session=herdr-1793585223-1761548-25344` (large ~107K-token full-prompt reprocess; lease_extended_during_prefill at 05:27:22/05:28:07/05:28:19) — the slot is genuinely busy with live work.
3. The first residual poll (05:31:18.459) is 6 ms BEFORE `Stream started: provider=local session=herdr-1793596937-2342287-16191 turn=993bed20` (05:31:18.465) + `prefill_progress_measured` (31K tokens) — a second live local dispatch starts at that exact second.
4. All 65 residual polls (05:31:18 → 05:33:07) read `available_slots=1`, `capacity_hint=saturated`, `local_in_flight_requests=0`, `local_owner_session_id=None`, `local_active_query=false`, `slots_detail_stale=false`: a busy slot whose in-flight/owner attribution the status payload does **not** reflect during prefill.
5. Same shape reproduces live (2026-11-02 09:06): `available_slots=1` + `saturated` + `in_flight=0` + `owner=None` for several seconds while slot prefill for a REAL dispatch is in flight (owner + in_flight appear ~9 s later). Also observed: `available_slots=2` + `saturated` with fresh detail (09:06:41) — the counts-stale family (LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA).

## Users

- **Proxy operator / on-call.** Reads `/llama/local/status` to decide whether the machine is genuinely busy. A `saturated` hint from a prefilling slot misdirects triage and hides real saturation (alarm fatigue).
- **Routing policy / dispatchers** (including the herdr downtime worker). `saturated` steers work to cloud/remote providers; a false `saturated` from live work causes avoidable paid fallback and, historically, starvation of the downtime dispatcher (LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM).
- **Measurement analyst** re-running `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py`. Needs every residual poll attributable, otherwise the next re-measurement is as unexplained as this one.

User stories:

- As an on-call operator, when a slot is prefilling a real local dispatch, I want the status payload to say so (owner/in-flight set), so I don't misread capacity.
- As the herdr downtime worker, when a slot is doing live prefill work, I accept `saturated`; when it is not, I want a signal that distinguishes it, so I don't fall back to paid providers needlessly.
- As a measurement analyst, I want the widened attribution reason set to cover every residual poll, so re-measurements reach zero or full attribution.

## Goal (re-targeted)

Reconcile **slot-occupancy vs in-flight/owner attribution in the status builder** so a slot that is genuinely busy with live local work (prefill in progress for a real dispatch) reads its live-work attribution (`local_in_flight_requests`/`local_owner_session_id`/`local_active_query` or an equivalent signal) instead of `capacity_hint=saturated` with empty live-work fields. This is **NOT** the post-cancel draining-ghost the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM fix targets — extending `abandoned_busy` to the session-eviction path would not close this class.

## Work

1. Root-cause the status-builder lag: why does a slot prefilling for a real local dispatch read `in_flight=0` / `owner=None` (busy slot, but no live-work attribution)? Check against the counts-stale family LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA first (the 09:06:41 `available_slots=2` + `saturated` shape may be the same family).
2. Fix the status builder (or the residual classifier) to attribute live work during prefill — truthful-status contract LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM must not be weakened (`some` live work must still read `saturated`).
3. Re-run the measurement over a comparable night (same invocation shape as `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-01_night-post-deploy/run_measurement.sh`) to confirm the residual drops toward 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A slot prefilling a real local dispatch never reports `capacity_hint=saturated` with `local_in_flight_requests=0` / empty owner on fresh slot detail; it either carries the live-work attribution or reads a live-work hint.
- AC2: A pool with live work still reads `saturated` (truthful-status contract LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM unweakened) — existing deterministic tests pass unchanged.
- AC3: Over a fresh closed night window, saturated-without-live-work polls are 0, or every residual is attributed with the widened reason set.
- AC4: The 5 unattributable polls from the 2026-11-01 night are either attributed via extended evidence (see LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR) or provably absent.

## Constraints

- Truthful-status contract LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM must not be weakened: a pool with live work must still read `saturated` (`some` live work, even unfinalised during prefill, is still live).
- Do not duplicate LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR (attribution extension for unattributable polls) — reference it; AC4 here is bounded by "or provably absent".
- Measurement windows must be comparable in invocation shape to the 2026-11-01 night run (`run_measurement.sh`) and free of proxy-process restarts inside the window (the 2026-11-01 window's first 86 min were served by an earlier process).

## Existing state

The abandoned_busy annotation (LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM, landed on `dev`) already annotates post-cancel draining slots — 367 polls / 2.06 % read `abandoned_busy`. The residual class under this item is distinct: a **busy** slot (live prefill) whose live-work fields the status builder leaves empty. The counts-stale shape (`available_slots=2` + `saturated` with fresh detail) is tracked separately in LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA and may or may not be the same family (overlap check required before re-measuring).

## Desired change

The status payload for a slot prefilling a real local dispatch must expose its live-work attribution (or an equivalent live-work hint) instead of `saturated` with empty owner/in-flight fields — either in the status builder (`proxy/proxy/observability.py`) or, if root-cause shows the read path is stale, via the residual classifier's widened reason set.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — capacity hint status builder (live-work attribution during prefill)
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` — measurement tool / residual classifier
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — slot-polling helpers (multi-slot iteration, per LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L)
- `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-11-01_night-post-deploy/verdict.txt` and `saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv` — evidence (72 rows; 65 mis-attributed to `session_evicted`)
- `proxy/docs/per-slot-status-verification.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md` — documented `abandoned_busy` semantics (update on behaviour change)

## Risks and assumptions

- (Risk) The `available_slots=2` + `saturated` shape may belong to the counts-stale family (LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA); if root-cause confirms overlap, do not duplicate that fix inside this item — link it and keep this item's scope to prefill attribution.
- (Risk) Fixing attribution inside the builder while keeping `saturated` truthful for genuinely busy pools (AC2) is the core tension; existing deterministic tests are the guard.
- (Risk) A re-measurement night with a proxy-process restart inside the window invalidates comparability; pick a restart-free window.
- (Risk) AC4 depends on LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR (currently blocked); if it stays blocked, satisfy AC4 via "provably absent" under the widened reason set.
- (Assumption) The 09:06:41 `available_slots=2` + fresh-detail shape is the counts-stale family until proven otherwise.
- (Scope-creep guard) Any additional residual classes discovered during root-cause go to new linked work items, not this item's scope.

## Related work

- discovered-from: LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1 (verification item whose verdict this files)
- LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM — original draining-slot annotation fix (this is a different residual class)
- LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR — attribution extension for unattributable residual polls (reference, do not duplicate)
- LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM — truthful-status contract
- LP-0MVXSX0TZ00798KA — counts-stale family (overlap check required)
- LP-0MRO4U5O1008TLFU / LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L — multi-slot polling tests/fix for `poll_slots_for_model()` (completed; polling iteration context)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No interview required — the item was re-targeted with sufficient evidence by the LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1 verdict session and the LP-0MVUTYHG7001S6BM implementation session before this intake. Evidence above is the answer record (log-analysis timestamps and live reproduction 2026-11-02 09:06, sourced from `/var/log/llama-proxy` and the status payloads cited in the Evidence section).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MVVXGMGB004DUGR** – Attribute saturated-without-live-work residual polls (blocked)
- **LP-0MRO4U5O1008TLFU** – Write multi-slot tests for poll_slots_for_model() (completed)
- **LP-0MRO4U5NT005DP6L** – Fix poll_slots_for_model() to iterate all slots (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — matched: 0mvutyhg7001s6bm, abandoned, absent, ac1, ac2 (+175 more)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — matched: 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, 0mvutyhg7001s6bm, abandoned, absent, ac1 (+170 more)
- `proxy/README.md` — matched: 0mvksxr4p001v0cm, abandoned, absent, ac1, ac2 (+166 more)

## Plan (2026-11-02, plan skill)

### Root cause confirmed (log-analysis of `/var/log/llama-proxy`, 2026-11-01/02)

The residual is a **per-session dispatch-record teardown race**, not a stale read
path and not a missing attribution reason:

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py::_decrement_local_active_queries` closes a *turn*
by writing `local_dispatch_records[(endpoint, session_id)]["active"] = False` and
`expires_at = now + lease_timeout`, logging `lease_renewed`. When the next turn
of the **same session** has already re-acquired that shared record key, the late
teardown of turn N clears turn N+1's live-work attribution for its whole
prefill:

```text
05:31:07,383  Stream finished: ... provider=local session=herdr-1793596937   (turn N ends)
05:31:07,675  [local] POST ... (turn N+1 admitted, same session, same record key)
05:31:08,008  lease_renewed session=herdr-1793596937 timeout=30s            (turn N teardown, LATE)
05:31:13,015  local_active_queries counter recovered: reset from 1 to 0 (0 active dispatch records)
05:31:18,459  status_request avail=1 hint=saturated in_flight=0 owner=None slots_detail_stale=false latency_ms=3000
05:31:18,465  Stream started: provider=local session=herdr-1793596937       (first byte after 10.8 s prefill)
```

Control: polls at `05:33:4x` (same session, prefill with **no** teardown inside
it) read `local_in_flight_requests=1`, `local_owner_session_id=herdr-1793596937-…`.

`_release_local_dispatch` carries the mirror hazard: it `del`s the record
unconditionally, so a late abandonment release can delete a newer dispatch's
record outright.

### Attribution of the 72 residual polls (parent AC4)

- **65/72** (`05:31:18` → `05:33:07`): the cross-turn teardown race above, one
  looping agent session (`herdr-1793596937-…`) whose turn boundaries recur every
  7-18 s. The `session_evicted` cause in the tool's CSV is the 600 s
  nearest-event mis-attribution already documented on LP-0MVUVHBZH007INL1.
- **5/72** ("unattributable"): the **same class**, now attributed:
  `22:12:55,240 [local] POST` → `22:12:55,282 lease_renewed` → polls
  `22:12:57`-`22:13:00`; `23:02:16,450 [local] POST` → `23:02:16,478
